nostr-tools 2.25.0

Included exports: generateSecretKey, getPublicKey, finalizeEvent, verifyEvent
(from nostr-tools/pure), SimplePool (from nostr-tools/pool), wrapEvent/unwrapEvent
(from nostr-tools/nip17), getConversationKey (from nostr-tools/nip44), GiftWrap
(from nostr-tools/kinds), schnorr (from @noble/curves/secp256k1.js, nostr-tools'
own signing dependency — used for the raw prekey signature in PLAN.md §6.2/§6.3,
which is not itself a Nostr event).

Build deviation from PLAN.md §4.2 step 1: the jsDelivr `+esm` endpoint
(cdn.jsdelivr.net) and every alternative CDN tried (esm.sh, unpkg.com,
cdn.skypack.dev) were unreachable from this sandboxed build environment
(network policy blocks them; only registry.npmjs.org and a few other package
registries are allowed). Produced the same kind of artifact — a single
self-contained browser ESM bundle, no runtime CDN dependency — by installing
nostr-tools@2.25.0 from the npm registry and bundling the six exports above
with esbuild (--bundle --format=esm --platform=browser --target=es2020
--minify) instead. Verified with a smoke test exercising every exported
function (event sign/verify, NIP-17/59 wrap+unwrap round trip, NIP-44
conversation-key symmetry, schnorr sign/verify, SimplePool construction)
before committing. No protocol or security spec (PLAN.md §6/§7) was changed;
only the packaging method for step 1 of §4.2 differs. Flagged per PLAN.md
§14 rule B.

Rebuild recipe (if a future update is needed):
  npm install nostr-tools@2.25.0 esbuild
  echo '
  export { generateSecretKey, getPublicKey, finalizeEvent, verifyEvent } from "nostr-tools/pure";
  export { SimplePool } from "nostr-tools/pool";
  export { wrapEvent, unwrapEvent } from "nostr-tools/nip17";
  export { getConversationKey } from "nostr-tools/nip44";
  export { GiftWrap } from "nostr-tools/kinds";
  export { schnorr } from "@noble/curves/secp256k1.js";
  ' > entry.js
  npx esbuild entry.js --bundle --format=esm --platform=browser --target=es2020 --minify --outfile=nostr-tools.js
